newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Feb consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Feb consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted February consumer price index rose 0.1 percent in the month and 2.2 percent in the year to 137.3, Statistics Canada said Friday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Feb Jan
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.1 +0.1
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.5 +1.8

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month and the undadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 2.2 percent year-over-year rise in the all- items and 1.7 percent rise in the core CPI.
The core CPI rise of 1.5 percent was well within the Bank of Canada's target inflation range of one to three percent.

Statistics Canada said the month-on-month 0.1 percent increase in the unadjusted CPI was due to higher prices for clothing, footwear, gasoline, food, travel tours and traveller accommodation. Food rose 0.2 percent and energy costs rose 0.7 percent due mainly to a 1.5 increase in gasoline prices.
Since February of last year, motorists have seen a 10.8 percent rise in the price of gasoline, the federal agency said.

The February increases were largely offset by lower air fares -- which bucked the trend from previous years and plunged nine percent -- as well as lower prices for owned accommodation and telephone service.

The year-over-year unadjusted increase of 2.2 percent was traced to higher prices for energy, food, vehicle insurance coverage, new vehicles and university tuition. The climb was offset partly by continuing declines in mortgage interest charges, which fell 5.1 percent during the year. Energy rose 7.2 percent on the year, accounting for a quarter of the index's yearly rise, Statscan said. Food prices rose 2.4 percent on the year.
